verdict.rationale: Alloy documents an Events API for submitting transaction events, routing them to Source Workflows for monitoring, and transaction-monitoring workflows; customer identifiers are implied by its External Entity ID documentation. Counterparty identifiers are never mentioned, and nothing documents rejected input: there is no validation-error, error-code, or resubmission guidance. The 206 warnings describe missing vendor data in an evaluation, not a rejected request. missing for 10: documented counterparty identifier fields on transaction events, validation/rejection error responses and a recovery or resubmission path, a transaction payload schema, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can ingest transactions with customer and counterparty identifiers and recover from rejected input

citations.quote: Alloy supports dozens of use cases like interdicting on transactions
any event can be submitted for additional monitoring by mapping the event type to a Source Workflow
Monitors transaction events in real time or at scheduled times to detect suspicious activity
